solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Company gets passionate feelings about Republican groups

indicators.note: about means around, so the feelings word wraps around the single letter

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
to have the hots is to feel strong desire
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: A firm finds itself lusting after Republican factions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohorts are bands or companies of people, originally Roman military divisions, so they are groups.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Clegg, ultimately wedged in under him, snapped "What a great thing!"

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the name is used
something wedged in is jammed inside, so that letter goes inside the following words
something snapped is broken, so the combined letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the surname Clegg

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg, squeezed beneath a coalition partner, bursts out with sarcastic praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg was the Liberal Democrat deputy prime minister in David Cameron's coalition government, often seen as junior to him.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is informal slang for something remarkable or outstanding of its kind.

clue.text: Liberal chatter – it needs to have teeth

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters are given freedom to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Liberal politicians' talk needs to be backed by real bite to mean anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel or bar engaged by a pawl, so it cannot work without its teeth.

clue.text: In case two males climax

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second, the case around it

blocks.note: a suit is a law case
M abbreviates male, twice

explanation.surface: A smutty scene: two men reaching a climax together.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point or peak of something, which is what a climax is.

clue.text: Cyclops is doubly repulsed by Civil Service heads – apes!

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the words are read backwards
heads are the leading letters, so only the initial of each word is kept

blocks.note: the setter Cyclops calls himself I, and 'I is' contracts to I'M
doubly means the same piece is used a second time
the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: The setter is twice turned away by top civil servants, whom he dismisses as apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' means the reversed piece appears twice in a row. Cyclops is the setter, so he stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy them, which is exactly what someone who mimics another does.

clue.text: Heartless Lewinsky wants to hassle 'er boss

indicators.note: without a heart, all the middle is removed and only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: Monica Lewinsky; the outer letters of her first name
to nag is to pester or hassle
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted Monica Lewinsky wants to harass her employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewinsky must first be turned into her first name, Monica, before its heart is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager runs a team or business, so is the boss of those working under them.

clue.text: Wicked Private Eye in charge?

blocks.note: Private Eye is a magazine, a mag for short
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Would the magazine running things be an evil prospect?
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is the satirical British magazine in which this crossword appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang terms of approval meaning brilliant or excellent, as in a wicked or magic goal.

clue.text: MP hugged by whip, which is rather cheesy

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun

indicators.note: something hugged by another is wrapped inside it, so the first word sits within the second

blocks.note: a cat o' nine tails is a whip
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP getting a cuddle from the party whip is a bit cringeworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: A party whip enforces discipline in Parliament, but here the whip is a cat o' nine tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese, so a thing that is very much made of cheese.

clue.text: Thatcher, Mitty-like, concealing the loner

indicators.note: concealing means holding out of sight, so the answer lies inside the run of words

blocks.note: the end of the surname and start of Mitty, run together

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, a daydreamer like Walter Mitty, secretly hides a solitary nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is a fictional fantasist who lives in daydreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives apart from society by choice, the archetype of a solitary person who shuns company.

clue.text: High after working in Missouri – a state Bill Clinton found hard to maintain?

definitions.text: a state Bill Clinton found hard to maintain?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the abbreviation for the state that follows
after puts the first-named piece at the end, behind the rest

blocks.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri
a machine that is working is on
high meat or game is gamy, starting to go off

explanation.surface: Getting high after a job in Missouri, apparently a place Clinton couldn't stay faithful in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks geographical, like Missouri, but means condition. Bill Clinton's affairs, notably with Monica Lewinsky, make the definition a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Monogamy is the condition of having only one sexual partner, which Clinton notoriously failed to keep up.

clue.text: If thing's splattered with gin, it's common in most parties

indicators.note: splattered things are scattered messily about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe and s
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spilt gin is a familiar sight at most drinks parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests social parties with drinks; the definition means political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Infighting is squabbling among members of the same group, a regular feature of political organisations.

clue.text: (& 1dn.) 'Reveal all' orgasm's on celeb's top list

definitions.note: The quoted phrase is in headline style, where tense is routinely dropped, so a present-tense headline can stand for the past-tense answer.

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece comes before the rest
the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: read as orgasm has, i.e. reached a climax
the first letter of celeb
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A tabloid confession tops a celebrity's list of revelations.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is to confess everything, owning up fully to what one has done or hidden.

clue.text: Taxing wife at a great age

blocks.note: W abbreviates wife
being eighty is being at a great age

explanation.surface: An elderly wife proves demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty is serious and burdensome, demanding effort, which is what a taxing task is.

clue.text: Struggle to conclude each victory against Labour's right wing

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its right-hand end, so its final letters are kept

blocks.note: to end is to conclude
EA abbreviates each
V for victory
the last three letters of Labour

explanation.surface: Political attempts to finish each win over Labour's right faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' simply sets one piece next to the next. 'Right wing' looks political but selects the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to try hard, to strive or make an effort, so it is to struggle.

clue.text: Prince gets sweats for "architecturally-distinguished place"

blocks.note: PR is an abbreviation for prince
an ague is a fever with shivering and sweating fits

explanation.surface: A prince, probably Charles, works himself into a lather over a fine building.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles was famous for his strong opinions on architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech capital is celebrated for its Gothic and Baroque buildings and preserved old town.

clue.text: Medal one placed centrally on chest, being a business failure

indicators.note: placed in the middle, so that letter is put inside the word

blocks.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour
the Roman numeral for one
the bust is the chest

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on someone's chest marks a firm collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bust is to become bankrupt, so a firm doing so is in the process of collapsing financially.

clue.text: Hurd put out early day brief for the City

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or upset, so the name's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
AM is the short form for the morning hours

explanation.surface: Douglas Hurd, annoyed, issues a short morning statement to the City.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Hurd was a Conservative Foreign Secretary; 'the City' suggests London's financial district but here is a cathedral city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Durham is a city in north-east England, home to a cathedral and a university.

clue.text: To get set up in office, isn't accepting Trump's ultimate power ring

definitions.text: To get set up in office

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter of the name is taken
accepting means taking in, so the following pieces go inside

blocks.note: ain't is a colloquial isn't
the last letter of Trump
P abbreviates power
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Getting into office without accepting Trump's final power base.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to assign them a job or position, installing them in an official role.

clue.text: Conservative hearts break when trapped by Tory extremes

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters are taken
something trapped by another is caught inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Tory
H abbreviates hearts, the card suit
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Conservative hearts are broken when caught out by extreme Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks political, like the Tories in the wordplay, but means careful with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrifty means spending carefully and avoiding waste, a cautious or sparing attitude to money.

clue.text: It should facilitate a quick withdrawal, tickling her lots

definitions.text: It should facilitate a quick withdrawal

indicators.note: tickling makes someone squirm and wriggle, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saucy hint that tickling her a lot helps someone pull out fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The withdrawal is the drawing of a gun, not a sexual one.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a case worn on the belt that holds a pistol ready to be drawn fast.

clue.text: Jonathan almost turned round dispute? No joy

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
turned round means facing the other way, so the shortened name is read backwards

blocks.note: Jonathan Ross, the British TV and radio presenter
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Jonathan nearly backed down from an argument, but had no success.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan is a first name standing for the surname of the well-known chat-show host Jonathan Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is deep sadness, the absence of joy; 'no joy' also reads as slang for failure.

clue.text: see 24dn.
Crap written about Genesis's lead sad song

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so the first letter is taken
written about means written around, so the first word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: dire means dreadful, crap
the first letter of Genesis

explanation.surface: A rude review of a gloomy track by the band Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis is the British rock band, though it could also be the Bible's first book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful piece of music, originally a funeral lament for the dead.

clue.text: Promiscuous Rolf involved with "Private Eye-gate"

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so all the letters are mixed together

blocks.note: taken as written
a private eye is a private investigator, a PI
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Rolf Harris was an entertainer jailed for sexual offences; '-gate' is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligate means recklessly extravagant or dissolute, so it covers loose sexual behaviour too.

clue.text: (& 21ac.) Democrat underneath high-profile Republican vehicle, which is an advantage

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies underneath comes later, so that letter goes at the end

blocks.note: Donald Trump, the most prominent Republican
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A Democrat trapped beneath a Republican's car is an image of party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A trump card is a decisive resource held in reserve, which gives its holder the upper hand.

clue.text: Palace type reportedly copped one with Brenda

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is told by word of mouth, so a sound is wanted

blocks.note: copped is slang for caught; in British speech the two sound the same
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A royal hanger-on apparently got caught with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British accents 'caught' and 'court' are said alike. Private Eye called Queen Elizabeth II Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends at a royal court, so is someone found at the palace.

the article a, then U, the letter preceding V in the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: 'V sign' looks like one phrase, the rude British two-fingered gesture, but the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac in astrology.

taken as written
